title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion, UCLA on 1973-11-17
lineage: SBD> MR> C> DAT> CDR> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording of a peak‑'73 show highlighted by the legendary Playin’ > Uncle John’s > Morning Dew sandwich and stellar Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The November ’73 performance is consistently praised for its tight playing, fluid segues and a second‑set that rides on a smoking Playin’ > UJB > Morning Dew > UJB > Playin’ “sandwich.”  Reviewers note the soundboard source is crisp and clear (with only minor hiss or splice artifacts), making the musical highs—HC Sunshine, China Cat → I Know You Rider, Eyes of the World, Brown‑Eyed Women, Sugar Magnolia and the sandwich itself—truly shine.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 90 % of reviews are 5‑star with consistent praise for both performance and sound quality; only a few low‑rating outliers mention minor gaps or personal preferences.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with slight high‑frequency hiss that can be tamed; occasional splice around the UJB segment and some blank gaps between tracks noted but not detracting from overall enjoyment.

standout_songs: Playing in the Band > Uncle John's Band > Morning Dew > Uncle John's Band > Playing (sandwich)
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds nicely with HC Sunshine and strong early jams; second set is a showcase of seamless transitions, especially the Playin’ sandwich and an energetic Eyes of the World that keep the momentum rolling.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry’s meandering yet purposeful jam leading into the sandwich, his “gentle shred” on Uncle John’s and his intense intensity throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is praised for adding spice under the jams – “blowing bombs” in Morning Dew and locking in tightly with Jerry’s leads.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir gets nods for “slashing” background guitar work and strong vocal harmonies, especially on Brown Eyed Women and Sugar Magnolia.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's playing is noted as solid (especially on China Cat → Rider) though a few mention his mix being low in certain moments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s hi‑hat work is praised for following Jerry’s intensity; overall drum interplay with Phil is described as tight and driving.
